newsitem.title: USA: States to get most of any tobacco insurance funds.
newsitem.headline: States to get most of any tobacco insurance funds.

text.p: Tobacco companies agreed Friday to turn over to the states 80 percent of any insurance proceeds they receive as part of a landmark settlement announced that day, Louisiana Attorney General Richard Ieyoub said Friday.

Ieyoub discussed that aspect of the landmark settlement reached in Washington at a news conference in Baton Rouge, La. He chaired the insurance committee during the tobacco talks and in March named more than 100 insurers as defendants in a lawsuit seeking to recover Louisiana medical costs of treating smokers, using the state's direct-action statute.
The direct-action law allows injured parties to file suit directly against insurance companies which have insured the people or businesses responsible for their injuries.

However, the tobacco companies themselves have so far refrained from suing their insurers for product liability coverage, in part because it would have involved turning over the control of their legal defence to their insurers.
